implementation_adaptations.shared_life_down_debug.hpp and runtime.c: src/ddda_mcp/death.py and agent.js; source hashes reviewed in upstream_contract.json
implementation_adaptations.existing build/deploy/save primitives: src/ddda_mcp/harness.py and regression.py (private receipts and cleanup)
implementation_adaptations.session.cpp developer assignment and str: control.js and control.py (bounded fixed actions, expiring provider ownership)
implementation_adaptations.party_inventory_snapshot.js, grab_regist: world.js (callback-only, copied values, bounded opaque identities)
implementation_adaptations.native_offline.cpp and network_guard.cpp: sdk.py generates a minimal offline bridge from immutable sources; standalone.js observes callbacks without co-op runtime

components.strategy: adapt into inert functions with explicit paths and bounded output
derive searchable index; preserve authoritative upstream records
wrap behind exclusive coordinator; do not expose arbitrary evaluate
extract definition-only readers; runtime_api.js starts synthetic input and must not be loaded wholesale
invoke pinned scripts in isolated checkout through curated typed recipes
reuse existing local database and bounded exports; serialize database access
later-stage adaptation with ownership, backup and game-closed checks
reuse pins where compatible; retain notices when copying code

components.name: reviewed gameplay ownership and world layouts

components.strategy: Compile exact offline guard sources into an isolated minimal bridge; no co-op gameplay implementation

notes: Git blob identities identify committed source, not local working-tree bytes.
Resolve the pinned commit and verify each blob before adapting or executing it.
Experiment documents may include historical claims; retain evidence scope and build identity.
Private evidence, game binaries, saves, tools and decompiler databases are excluded.
Do not load research/runtime_api.js for read-only status: it starts a synthetic-input timer.

config/ddcoop.ini.text:
; DDDA local pawn co-op settings. Close the game before editing; restart to apply.
; Supports Fighter, Mage, Ranger, Sorcerer, Strider and Warrior. Two XInput controllers by default.
; Use 0 = off and 1 = on. Invalid, unknown or duplicate entries disable co-op
; and explain the problem in ddcoop-runtime.log beside DDDA.exe.

[coop]
enabled=1
; Allow P2 to start NPC conversations, including shops and skill menus; P2 owns those menus.
; Restart the game after changing this setting. Default is on; set to 0 to disable.
p2_npc_interaction=1
; Experimental online features. Default 0 keeps the native offline lock.
; Keep 0 while the launcher is omitted: untested, possible account ban, at your own risk.
; A saved 1 persists across launches. Set 0 and restart to restore the lock.
online_mode=0
; AI research only. Keep 0 when playing with real controllers.
developer_input=0
; Deprecated compatibility key. Mage admission no longer depends on this value.
; Keep 0; developer_input remains a separate research-only provider setting.
experimental_mage=0
; P1/P2 separation limit in engine-native distance units. Range: 1000 to 20000.
max_distance=5000
; At the limit, release P2 to native AI or teleport P2 to the Arisen.
distance_action=ai

[input]
; Optional: P1 uses native mouse/keyboard and one XInput controller is reserved for P2.
; Default 0 uses two controllers. Restart after changing; controller swapping is disabled at 1.
; At 1, P1 owns inventory, NPC dialogue, shops and skill menus; P2 Back/View and Talk are disabled.
; P2 holds Start/Menu to join; the controller can occupy any XInput slot, including slot 0.
p1_keyboard_mouse=0
; P2 holds Start/Menu for this many milliseconds. Range: 500 to 3000.
join_hold_ms=1000
; P2 sticks only. Range: 0.05 to 0.45. Raise to suppress stick drift.
; Joining and recovery also treat sticks inside these deadzones as released.
movement_deadzone=0.245
camera_deadzone=0.24

[camera]
; P2 only. P1 uses the normal game options. Sensitivity range: 0.25 to 3.0.
horizontal_sensitivity=1.0
vertical_sensitivity=1.0
invert_horizontal=0
invert_vertical=0
; P2 vertical field of view in degrees. Range: 40 to 75.
; Native game/dinput8 FOV options affect P1; change this value for P2 and restart.
field_of_view=65
; P2 orbit distance. Range: 160 to 380 game units, or 0 for a native sample.
; 0 samples P1's distance when P2's orbit initializes or the actor/scene changes.
; It does not track later P1 distance changes; same-world rejoin retains the orbit.
; Obstruction collision can shorten either setting automatically.
distance=380
; vertical = P1 left, P2 right (side-by-side). horizontal = P1 top, P2 bottom.
; Close the game and restart to apply a layout change.
split_layout=vertical

[feedback]
; Show assignment and Offline status in the game window title.
status_caption=1
; Show the P2 skill list while a skill modifier is held. Status notices stay visible.
skill_hud=1
; Show the other player's pawn sigil, including an off-screen direction arrow.
partner_sigils=1
; Show the shared-life heart and remaining count when shared_lives is enabled.
; Aid prompts and persistence-failure warnings remain visible when this is off.
shared_life_hud=1
; P2 enemy health bars. Native rendering behavior remains under verification.
p2_enemy_health_bars=1
; P2 ally health bars, including optional visibility in the P2 pane.
p2_ally_health_bars=0

[recovery]
; Restore P2 to full health when native Aid revives them. Disabled by default.
full_health_revive=0
; Enable shared Arisen/main-pawn revival, including Aid for the Arisen. Default on.
; Set 0 to restore native death/revival rules. Full-health P2 healing above is separate.
; If both players are down, the game still ends, including with endless lives.
shared_lives=1
; Endless revival entitlements, default on. No life is spent or exhausted at 1.
; Set 0 to use the finite pool below. Restart after changing either option.
; Toggling endless preserves the finite balance; completed inn rest refills it.
endless_lives=1
; Finite shared pool maximum, 0 to 99. Spent lives persist in this installation.
; At endless_lives=0 each down spends one life; the next down at zero ends the game.
; ddcoop.shared-lives.state is separate from game saves; loading/New Game does not refill it.
; Changing the maximum clamps remaining lives; completed inn rest refills them.
shared_life_count=3

; With online_mode=0 (default), co-op forces Offline and blocks game transport.
; Leaving co-op does not reconnect a running process. Restart to change modes.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.text:
# Architecture and research boundaries

## Optional NPC dialogue ownership — 1.5.1-rc7

`[coop] p2_npc_interaction=0` defaults OFF; restart applies changes. When enabled,
five signature-pinned native adapters admit the controlled main pawn to ordinary
NPC selection/dispatch and observe start, root claim and root cleanup. They retain
native eligibility and transaction recipients; they never replace the Arisen
identity. Special quest interaction variants remain excluded. See EXP071.

`dialogue_menu.hpp` owns the conversation lease separately from inventory.
Per-invocation native tokens associate claims with the initiating controller;
the claimed NPC/world root survives child shop, inventory and skill screens.
Only the initiator receives raw native navigation. Controller generation changes
revoke P2 ownership and allow neutral P1 handback without forgetting the root.
Closing requires root removal, input release and both actors' post-original
consumer neutralization before gameplay resumes. Inventory child closure cannot
release the outer conversation. All five optional hooks are absent when OFF.
Native conversation camera framing remains based on the Arisen.

EXP072 adds Talk1 to the copied B-interaction prompt publication at the existing
B6EBB2 pre-B observer. Typed native NPC/scene readiness is bracketed; no proximity
search or native function call is added. Item capacity policy remains6/10 only.
The HUD shares the existing bounded-age/one-pending-input prompt lane and rejects
Talk when the optional dialogue setting is off.

## Shared inventory ownership — 1.5.1-rc1

`shared_menu.hpp` owns a value-only controller lease for native inventory. A
fresh P2 Back/View edge, armed by releasing Back while ownership is healthy,
requests one logical XInput0 opening pulse even while movement is held.
Opening strips other controls; native menu navigation waits for P2 neutral.
Typed native inventory activation and opener release admit raw P2 navigation;
Session keeps controller-to-actor bindings fixed. Other native menus are P1-owned,
except the optional NPC conversation lease described above.

`shared_menu_native.hpp` tracks opaque inventory incarnation tokens. Five
ordinary typed thiscall wrappers observe initialization/update/close/cleanup/
destruction; retained identities are never dereferenced outside callbacks.
The UI persists across closes, so active +1C8=0 update after absence advances its
serial. Close entry neutralizes input before native execution. Both canonical
actors' movement/button callbacks clear proven outputs after their originals;
fresh gameplay, released pads and four required consumer acknowledgements finish
the return. Fault/world/device changes cancel ownership; a still-open inventory
can return to P1 after neutral release. The exact EXP024 pause flag tuple blocks
opening during stale canonical actor observations. See EXP055 for pins, ABI,
source-review corrections and bounded native acceptance.

## Native revival and ribbon state1.4.0

EXP-048 adds a pinned AFDB57 x86 bridge at native action129 initialization.
The adapter may replace only its stack-local heal fraction after current
controller, canonical pawn/action, world/generation, vocation and health checks.
Native888DA0 retains HP/white/saved-health mutation and limits. DefaultOFF and
busy/reentrant paths retain native behavior; terminal petrification is unchanged.
A separate completed-input timestamp supplies notice freshness independently of
poll throttling. HUD drawing explicitly owns WRAP0 and MULTISAMPLEMASK while
its full device-state block restores caller values. See EXP-048 and1.4.0
acceptance/delivery records for native and isolated evidence and limitations.

## XInput loader 1.2.1 — delivered 13 October 2026

`src/xinput_proxy.cpp` provides the exact XInput1.3 name/ordinal contract plus
CoopLoaderGetStatus@104. Its actual DllMain is inert. Initialization requires
the verified native controller-discovery returnDF9DC9, directly or from Windows
CaptureStackBackTrace(0,32), outside RtlIsThreadWithinLoaderCallout. Exact game
hash/live signatures, runtime canonical path/ABI identity and a single atomic
initialization attempt remain required. Steam overlay's captured ancestry passed
in native runs; wrappers hiding that frame safely leave co-op inactive. The
callback query does not prove absence of every arbitrary private/loader lock.

`src/system_xinput.cpp` resolves and validates an absolute system x86 module,
distinct from the local proxy, and retains it for process lifetime. Named-entry
admission closes and drains existing calls before MinHook changes; reentry never
waits. Cached logical calls enter the hooked backend entry, physical runtime
polling uses original trampolines. Ordinals100–103 use transparent x86 thunks;
they are outside the named admission contract. Missing backend in a cold loader
callback for these opaque signatures fast-fails rather than inventing an ABI.

Runtime exports separate build identity, initialization state and initialization.
Disabled/failure/in-progress states never masquerade as active; once transport
blocking is installed it stays pinned. Status ABI is212bytes, including bounded
diagnostic stack frames. Fixtures are isolated under xinput-proxy-fixture and
their test seams are absent from the production DLL. No upstream dinput8 source
was copied into the release. See EXP-046 and1.2.1 acceptance for exact evidence.

## Delivered 1.1.0 integration findings — 12 October 2026

The accepted Ranger path reuses the established bow and dagger native action
consumers and resource progression. Bounded evidence covers Ranger 400–408
activation/high routes and actual ring-derived ranks; ordinary P2 arrow target
HP subtraction is directly attributed in `private/research/ranger-sorcerer-20261012/c7r-final-arrow-summary.md`.
That separate ordinary shot does not establish damage from skill408 Great
Gamble. Its paired observer shows P2 stick-driven direction change while
movementMode remains0 and a per-effect physics rate change without changing
shared world time. Subsequent idle/recovery was seen, but not the exact effect
ending/destruction event, 2B12 transition, collision or target damage. No
unproved owner-flag change was added.


Root-confirmed native boundaries: Ranger is job8/longbow family11. The exact arrow type is vtable15F7B80, with direct P2 owner and origin
attribution and stored action02060002. Gamble steering additionally requires
resource15F7B40, category9 and variant0/2. The
Great Gamble birth lease at B1D71F binds skill408 effect to actor, resource,
epoch and generation; address reuse retires the lease and ended2B12 rejects
steering. P2 locomotion suppression expires 100ms after the last verified steer
consumer. Its per-effect physics rate moves .05→.03 over100 native frames, then
returns to1; any already lower native rate wins and shared world time is not
changed.

Sorcerer is job9/family6, distinct from Mage job3/family5. Rank2 applies only
to227–230;231/232 remain maximum rank1. Fulmination uses its dedicated typed
phase consumer, not the broad Mage channel path. These are bounded native
guards/dispatch facts summarized from EXP-044 and its reviewed captures, not a
claim that every Sorcerer effect or recipient outcome was verified.
The Sorcerer extension routes bounded base/high/shared and Grand native actions
through matched Mage-family behavior with rank/profile and native resource
checks. Evidence includes own-camera aim, placement/channel paths, bounded
self-enchantment/status applications and Holy P2-to-P1 application. It does not
prove every recipient or enemy outcome. Mage/Strider regression samples record
native actions and idle recovery with observers restored and zero observed
faults; they are targeted samples, not full matrices. See EXP-044 and its
private captures for per-route provenance and limitations.

All live extension checks used simulated XInput-provider input. Physical two-pad
acceptance, hot-plug and latency remain outside demonstrated behavior. The
architecture retains native ownership/cost/effect lifecycles and uses bounded
P2 adaptations only where the paired trace supports them. Horizontal split,
independent P2 inventory and online remain excluded.

Delivered native resource HUD (EXP-042): a private cockpit0_1 gauge reuses
native HP/ST/white-health helpers, sprite HP digits and borders. P1's live gauge
is borrowed only as an asset source within the awaited GUI job scope; no P1
nodes or actor globals are swapped. Snapshot epoch/generation guards identity;
zero-delta private property evaluation applies helper frames. Native E09D50
pane fitting is retained for matching P1/P2 scale. Private resources release
after native command consumption on pause/leave, and rebuild on return. The
old custom resource box is only a fault fallback; ability/aim panels remain.
Startup notice depends on fresh playable P1 observation and healthy offline
runtime, lasts at most15 seconds per process and hides on P2 join or gating.

Active owner-playtest correction (EXP-041): preserve P1's binding across actor/
stage replacement; retire P2 and require neutral plus fresh Start for rejoin.
Device topology/fault invalidation still retires both assignments. Native pawn
input receives raw stick axes for cliff states and unmodified B1000 after
vocation composition, with release protection for skill chords. Separation reads
max_distance/distance_action. Explicit recall runs inside the pawn movement
callback after neutralizing pending movement, using native collision correction,
ground/terrain checks, idle and canonical placement. No RPC/timer transforms.
Release the input lock around placement because native action dispatch reenters
hooks. Success retains P2 with a full-neutral barrier; refusal/timeout returns AI.
Shared pane geometry supports both orientations. Optional horizontal layout is
available with normal player settings; vertical remains the default. A bounded
native GUI lease fits both resource gauges, P1's palette and map without moving
projected world-label anchors. Exact owned positioned groups receive an X-scale
correction through the verified native setter; transforms, projection flags and
original geometry are restored after the callback, including exception paths.
Generic roots are never treated as positioned groups. Custom hint text uses a
compact row atlas so centered prompts remain visible beside left-aligned text.
See EXP069 for native C1/C2 evidence, exact-build provenance and coverage limits.

Fresh owned P2 action9 selects three original player continuations in B6FD20:
B70318 -> B70325 (heading basis), B705DE -> B705EB (normal confirmation ray),
B70747 -> B70754 (facing dot). Other actors/actions retain original trampolines.
No actor206D identity bits or2F94 AI path flags change. Naked bridges preserve
flags, GPRs, x87/SIMD and ESP, clear DF for the C++ predicate and restore original
DF before native continuation. The manifest pins all six entry/destination
signatures. Native52/53/54 and drop13/14 remain the action/physics authority.

Current Fighter extension (private RC4, 11 October): job1 admission and native
sword/shield input translation use complete equipment words and six equipped
slots. The typed Perfect Defense lease suppresses only the proven AI-only cancel
condition at the existing cancel bridge. Three signature-pinned AI producers
skip only automatic Just Guard intent for a fresh owned Fighter; residual intent
is cleared at the native input consumer. Manual guard timers and effects stay
native. Generic simple dispatch now passes actor and action with tested x86
state preservation. Final native Mage/Strider/Warrior regression passes. See
FIGHTER_INTEGRATION_20261011.md and PRIVATE_CANDIDATE_ACCEPTANCE_RC4.md.

Prior Mage extension (private RC3, 11 October): native staff category5 and
default vocation3 admission sit behind existing actor identity, freshness,
equipment, rank and offline checks. Typed Mage bridges supply native shot,
placement/marker, core and Levin target paths; bounded owner/lifetime leases
preserve native cleanup. Native progression/cost/effects remain authoritative.
See the Mage integration/review ledger and PRIVATE_CANDIDATE_ACCEPTANCE_RC3.md.
RC2 shared rendering and Strider/Warrior dispatch are carried forward unchanged;
DOF staysOFF and native HUD replacement remains deferred.

EXP-040 isolates the missing pawn body to native P1-camera opacity, with a
fixed-position visible/missing/reverse pair and both-view B6A070 observations.
Native 88BDC0 multiplies body base opacity (+2510) by P1-camera factors into
+2514 and updates opaque-routing bit3 in +8/+FAC. B6A070 propagates that value
to model+158 and model+108 bit30. These shared values reach both views.
The candidate scopes selected-pawn opacity and matching pass flags to the
existing synchronous P2 scene draw, before DB63E0 admission; restore floats
and only owned flag bits after native workers return, including SEH unwind.
It preserves native base opacity, fade state/timers, P1 behavior and P2 close/
aim body masks. No new engine hook or simulation call. Candidate verification
is recorded in EXP-040; static/synthetic checks are separate from live acceptance.

Releasec98c450f extends that scope to verified selected-pawn weapon and lantern
units, with at most32 leases restored in reverse order. Weapon type1602730 must
match selected parent30 and routing/fade sources2530/2534; use its own base2510.
Lantern type1603DD8 additionally requires the pawn3D6C back-reference; use parent
base2510 because native C27D20 has already multiplied P1 camera fade into lantern
base. Leave that lantern base untouched. Cloth's different model158 layout is
excluded. Normal/SEH, ownership, fractional fades and mask exclusions pass the
actual draw-adapter tests; bounded native visual regression is in EXP-040.

EXP-039 adds a research-only compact1Hz health recorder around the existing five
cached diagnostic readers. It has explicit PID/duration admission, independent
timer deadline, bounded rows/markers/events/errors and frozen stopped exports.
Captured run identity/reader and busy guards reject stale/cooperative callbacks;
marker attribution uses admission time before the potentially yielding read.
Full cumulative latency/elapsed snapshots belong at phase boundaries, external
process CPU/memory remain separate, and1Hz samples cannot certify transients.
The899-row pilot validates this bounded design, not a completed hour or area route.

The pilot initially left a visual uncertainty (resolved by EXP-040 above): right-pane pawn absence recovered
after both P1position and camera changed; fixed-position camera repeats remained
visible. P2camera distance227.664 weakens intentional close-body masking but does
not establish a native culling cause. Existing split draw interception extends
view bits only after other native admission/pose decisions; no new hook or flag
write is justified without a repeatable pair. The separate return follow-up ended
about201 units short while P1camera rotated during its two-second movement pulse.
Use short reprojected inputs and measured positions for the next reproduction.
See EXP-039 and its corrected visual notes; no render reliability pass is claimed.

EXP-038 keeps Present observation research-only and adds separate current-device
Reset accounting at COM slot16. Successful same-pointer Reset is now observed
at native return site DAFA92 and permanently invalidates that timing capture.
First-Reset admission continues while Present drains; final cleanup closes it
explicitly, detaches both listeners and verifies both prefixes and mapping
endpoints. A missing return or uncertain restoration retains ownership. Only the
first Reset invocation is accounted; later Resets and post-detach activity remain
outside the capture. Native fullscreen mode recovery restores split/HUD and P2
movement in the bounded experiment. See PRESENTATION_RESET_REVIEW.
Menu Present callers DAE5F6/DAE752/DAEE55 also show why a Device9 call stream must
not be labeled one sample per game frame. Five stationary off/on phases provide
descriptive whole-process CPU variation, not causal or whole-mod attribution.

EXP-037 now maps actual presentation separately from render/HUD boundaries.
Native DAED10 calls Device9 Present through renderer+0x98, COM slot17; sampled
returnsiteDAEE55 is on the main-device path. Optional SwapChain9 Present uses
renderer+0x440de4 records (stride28) when +0x440dfc>1. Sampled count1 and null
additional chain are state observations, not global exclusions. Device lost
sets renderer+0x433e54 bit0x10; exact Reset recovery remains unproven here.
The bounded research observer attaches at the COM entry while preserving the
existing Steam overlay jump chain; it adds no persistent runtime hook. Its
instrumented QPC calls cannot be treated as display-delivery or exact CPU timing.
Same-pointer Reset is invisible to pointer equality and must remain a separate
lifetime condition before longer/transition captures. See EXP-037 and its proof.

D26 / EXP-036 adds a separate research-only elapsed profiler. Seven ordinary C++
callback spans exclude their original native consumers. Nested measured children
have their own channel results and are removed from the parent's exclusive
categories. Native XInput/resource/camera helpers and HUD graphics remain visible
as separate categories; only selected explicit lock waits are separated. QPC
preemption and other nested waits remain in these elapsed values.

The fixed-capacity TLS tracker preserves logical unwind beyond its storage bound;
invalid roots publish diagnostics without channel data. A short metadata lock
serializes root admission with seal, then is released before callback work. A
completed outer root merges after its own callback locks are released. Cached
exports acquire only metadata locks, never game/runtime/split/HUD locks. No
thread registry or game pointers enter the2448/v1 ABI. Seal is nonblocking: reject
new roots, allow admitted nested work, seal permanently after the last completion.
A nonreturning root remains active/draining instead of silently disappearing.

Begin is research-gated and once per process; defaults and player configuration
cannot start profiling. Clock/start failures affect measurement, not ownership or
gameplay fault state. Admission/merge/control-lock contention lies outside spans;
valid timing roots are not proof of healthy gameplay. Off/on native observations
use the same instrumented build and are not a pre-patch overhead comparison.
This is partial41-hook coverage and no proven asynchronous frame attribution.
Whole-process GetProcessTimes samples and future presentation traces remain
separate evidence; summed thread elapsed cannot be labelled exact CPU/frame cost.

EXP-032 / Release2532b523 adds separate vocation admission evidence at both native
P2 input consumers. Identity-bound actor/Info/GS/epoch samples expire after150ms.
Strider2/Warrior7 are admitted; default-off experimental_mage admits only Mage3.
Known unsupported jobs release P2 through the existing explicit rejoin path.
Unknown evidence also releases when healthy native gameplay consumers continue,
avoiding an untracked suspended-AI242 to joined transition. Ordinary paused or
ineligible gameplay keeps its existing suspension. No native calls/hooks are
added; P1, native gameplay/health, generic AI provenance and distance hysteresis
stay separate. Independent cached notice/diagnostic APIs preserve old meanings.
Debug/Release26/26 pass. EXP-032 now passes273/273 bounded live checks for native
vocation changes/refusal/recovery and separate experimental Mage admission.
Warrior control implementation is now present; native verification and broad
shared-system acceptance remain open.

Release `982ac566` adds a separate Warrior primary-skill path for pawn job 7,
families 3 and 7. RB+X/Y/B selects the equipped native primary slots; RB wins
when both RB and LB are held, while LB alone retains ordinary basic actions.
Warrior has its own held-release gate, independent of the Strider bow gate.
Equipped-slot eligibility and native charge, release and cost behavior remain
authoritative, and the HUD labels the three RB buttons with equipped skill names.
The Release build passed 37/37 tests and is installed for controlled research;
native Warrior gameplay checks are pending, so this is implementation evidence,
not gameplay acceptance.

Release92d1d964 adds the EXP-031 separation policy at the existing native P2
movement consumer. It brackets both validated actors with world/identity reads,
normalizes coordinates by the shared origin offset, and publishes values under
the adapter lock. The poller never dereferences native objects. Before/after
brackets are not atomic rebasing; discontinuities require300ms reacquisition,
trusted values expire after150ms, and continuous excessive/near evidence needs
300ms. Unknown is distinct from confirmed excessive distance; fresh native
gameplay allows500ms unknown grace before release. Native pause/focus/health
retain their existing higher-priority gates and reset this grace.

D25: warn at2000, release P2 after sustained distance>2500, allow explicit
rejoin after sustained distance<=2000. These3D-distance thresholds are release
policy choices informed by EXP-018, not proven collision coverage. Release
keeps P1, advances assignment generation once and retains native consumers'
ownership flags until they emit neutral input. Healthy solo AI can record fresh
generic-action provenance, and solo->joined+1 reuses the proven handoff path.
No automatic suspended->joined AI handback is introduced. Recovery candidates
must release all controls and keep non-Start controls neutral through a fresh
Start hold. Each stick uses a1600-unit radial bound below every supported
movement/camera deadzone; disconnect/packet reset invalidates candidate history.

Separation notices render with the existing HUD submit boundary even when the
ordinary P2resource HUD is inactive/fullscreen. Resource diagnostics retain their
existing64-byte meaning; separate44/24-byte v1 cached ABIs expose policy/notice
state. Native menu/focus/health gates hide the notice. No engine placement,
global Arisen identity, native network behavior or settings override is changed.
25/25 Debug and Release pass; native acceptance is recorded separately.

Camera caveat found during verification: split::snapshot still copies the last
actor-consumer position. A timer sample straddling native rebasing can therefore
show old P2camera coordinates alongside new native actor coordinates. EXP-031
retains one10000-unit residual resolving28ms later. Two later opposite crossings
pass REBASE_RENDER_PROOF68/68: all2622 normal shadow-entry records align native
P2 camera pivot with the actor. These observations support correct rendering
coordinates at that boundary, but do not reconstruct the old timer sample or
prove every native pass/GPU output. No speculative camera patch is justified.

Initial-release P2 support is Strider and Warrior only (D24, 1 October).
Preserve the existing Mage implementation and research for later. A release
eligibility policy must refuse unsupported joins and revoke owned input safely
on unsupported vocation changes, leaving the native pawn AI intact with clear
feedback. Release2532b523 implements the admission policy with bounded synthetic
live validation in VOCATION_ADMISSION_PROOF. Both supported vocations still
need shared-system acceptance; Warrior now has a P2 implementation, but its
native gameplay verification is pending.

Installed Release cdcb5d93 adds native health eligibility inside engine_gate:
the existing actor+1D0C/+1D18 -> life node+8 chain must contain finite positive HP.
Missing/invalid/nonpositive health fails closed at the existing native consumers;
no new hook, engine call, signature, game write or ABI. Debug/Release24/24 passed.
SHARED_PAWN_LOSS_HEALTH_PROOF26/26 verifies brine death/recovery with raw HP:
control/view suspended by50ms, HUD101ms and native held intent0 under held RB+Y.
Ordinary Strider damage/Aid and movement/light recovery now pass25/25 plus15/15
(HEALTH_GATE_HELD_REVIVAL_PROOF/RECOVERY_PROOF). Same actor/Info/gen4 recovers
through native controller Aid, held input blocked and fresh skill cost preserved.
HEALTH_STRIDER_ACTIONS_PROOF25/25 adds healthy heavy/draw/sheath/primary/grab,
bow aim/selection/native65-stamina cost and light recovery on the revived actor.
HEALTH_MAGE_REGRESSION_PROOF41/41 adds the healthy compiled Frazil/Anodyne/
Fire Boon/Ingle regression. Existing consumers and signatures are unchanged;
read-only native spell/effect observations and provider inputs verify behavior.
No runtime change or new spell implementation is part of these regressions.
See EXP-028, PAWN_HEALTH_GATE_BUILD and preserved old failed19/20 trace.

Diagnostic menuGated is the last pawn engine_gate result, not an authoritative
P1 menu flag; it remains1 after a dead pawn is removed. Absent-pawn P1 navigation
must check the existing native scene/menu predicates instead. This changes only
the bounded provider helper, not runtime routing. Registry creation also precedes
the restored actor's first input consumer; retain both observations separately.

Release c3c1aa06 adds base Frazil at the existing pawn input and staff-init/
AI-source/cancel consumers. Each initialization revokes prior ownership; native
input edges bind a fresh lifetime after exact base-rank/parameter validation.
Current actor input renews it without depending on a target camera, because the
observed placement is caster-centered. Separate Frazil source phases prevent a
charge witness being reused for channel 6, which additionally requires the
current native effect's owner and B48270. No native action/resource/target writes,
new game calls or new hooks. A cached charge handoff uses the existing one-shot
native A policy on control loss. Phase HUD and pointer-free diagnostics added;
61 unique signatures/41 hooks, Debug/Release 24/24 and bounded live proof 70/70.
FRAZIL_REGRESSION_PROOF additionally verifies both-player independence and
bounded active-channel disconnect/leave/pause recovery on this build. Wider
combat/utility and long-pause behavior remain open. Native P1 Levin's separate
mode-1 ground marker lives at action+78 (Anodyne uses +74); its effects use
placement 2. The pawn placement branch's point/count/list route still requires
its own live proof before enabling P2 Levin.

Releasee065b07e adds the EXP-027 utility request bridge atB6BB40. It preserves
all native machine state around the callback and uses the existing AL0/RET4
refusal atB6BB49 only for proven55EE39/item64/action154/UseItem1574b80 state2
flags2/request154 with fresh, healthy, same-lifetime P2 base Boon state1/2 and no
pending/blocked request. Other actors/utilities/unowned actions follow the native
trampoline. No actor/producer/clock writes or new native calls. The native failed
handler cleanup and later retry are retained. One live owned startup collision
and A/retry/normal Ice/Thunder recovery pass33/33; repeated owned refusals and
broader utility regressions remain open.60 unique signatures/41 hooks; both
build configurations pass24/24 including full-state utility ABI paths. See
LANTERN_GUARD_BUILD, LANTERN_GUARD_PROOF and EXP-027. Earlier build descriptions
below are historical.

Undeployed diagnostic build268457eb extends existing StaffFailures to Fire/Ice/
Thunder Boon with the same identity/freshness reason codes and event kinds used

This is the intended release architecture. S2 implements a forwarding loader,
native actor adapter, assignment state machine and pinned offline guard in src/.
Two synthetic provider streams passed live-game isolation tests. Physical
two-controller acceptance and the finished HUD/gameplay are still pending.
See research/EXP-001-ENGINE-MAP.md and EXP-002-CONTROL-PROOF.md for verified offsets.

```text
Controller A / Controller B
        -> XInput provider -> assignment / edges / deadzones
        -> per-player command frames -> session state machine
        -> version-specific DDDA adapter -> native actor action system
                                      -> selected pawn AI-intent ownership
                                      -> scene / actor lifetime events
        -> diagnostics, replay fixtures and bounded status overlay
```

## Components

| Component | Responsibility | Failure behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Loader | Forward required DirectInput exports; defer initialization | Preserve normal game startup |
| Build resolver | Hash, module sections, unique signatures and ABI checks | Disable mod on mismatch |
| Input provider | Distinct XInput states, timestamps, edges and focus | Neutral state on lost device |
| Assignment | Explicit join, separate slots, uncertain identity handling | Require deliberate reassignment |
| Session | Solo, joining, controlled, suspended, leaving | Restore pawn AI at safe boundary |
| Offline lock | Force native Offline and deny DDDA transport before joining | Refuse co-op; no reconnect until process exit |
| Actor adapter | Resolve stable pawn identity; call native actions on game thread | Reject stale generation or bad state |
| AI ownership | Suppress selected pawn's voluntary intentions | Resume native AI, not a frozen actor |
| Camera adapter | Native Arisen/main-pawn viewports, P2 orbit and movement basis | Restore solo view when ownership/gates fail |
| Presentation | P2 status, assignment, boundaries, error status | No game-state ownership |
| Diagnostics | Version, events, timings, bounded ring log | Drop excess entries, never block game tick |

The S2 loader forwards the six verified system dinput8 exports and ordinals.
The executable imports DINPUT8.dll and XINPUT1_3.dll. XInput9_1_0 is used only by the
standalone controller probe. The runtime hooks the game's XInput 1.3 route,
polls physical devices through original trampolines, and exposes only one logical
P1 slot. The exact device initialization and isolation findings are in EXP-004.

## State model

EXP-027 Fire Boon presentation copies validated target coordinates and recipient
kind inside the existing pawn target consumer. The render snapshot reads cached
values only, with actor lifetime/epoch/generation and 100ms freshness guards.
No new engine-pointer dereference occurs in the HUD. The normal P2 view projector
clips the marker to that pane; state1/2 selects charging/ready text. The separate
48-byte v1 CoopGetBoonHudStatus keeps existing diagnostic ABIs unchanged. Native
spell contact/application remain engine-owned; no collision or buff writes were
added. Actual native ally application is now observed in a clear fixture.

EXP-027 separates ground and ally/self spell ownership. A post-native B44B00
callback binds a new Fire Boon lifetime only with completed pinned parameters
and fresh own intent. At B46C10, own-camera native selector queries run without
the runtime lock; identity, generation, lifetime and manager are revalidated
before own target writes. Target-list membership precedes node dereference.
No target at release supplies the proven native A input at the actor consumer.
Native tracking storage, stamina, collision, physics and effect application stay
engine-owned. CoopGetBoonStatus exposes a separate pointer-free64-byte v1 record;
CoopGetMageStatus remains the existing52-byte v1 ABI.

EXP-027 adds a native-ground query wrapper for release-gated LS recentering.
It invokes the validated B4B330 trampoline only inside the current pawn's target
consumer, after identity, lifetime, parameters, range and finite-position checks.
P2 camera direction supplies the desired point; native geometry supplies the
result. The wrapper preserves the full machine state. Marker walking suppression
uses current native actor/action ownership independently of camera freshness, so
stale aim data cannot fall through to walking. Target and cancellation consumers
continue to require fresh input/view. Native physics remains unchanged.

EXP-027 adds the narrow compiled Anodyne adapter. Six ABI bridges preserve all
native GPR/flags/x87/SIMD state around source observation, cancellation-return
policy, initial geometry scratch-input adjustment and own ground-target intent.
Native actor identity, world epoch, assignment generation, fresh input/view and
a serial bound at each native initial placement constrain every gameplay change.
Source observation runs before current input/camera refresh; it records validated
native provenance without requiring the old view to be fresh. Consumers still
require fresh control/view. Unknown cancellation producers invalidate provenance;
native A and other results remain unchanged. Native floor/obstruction queries,
marker smoothing/range handling, action transitions and stamina remain engine-owned.
Pause/loss clears the binding and release gate. Pointer-free Mage diagnostics do
not touch engine objects. See MAGE_ANODYNE_COMPILED_PROOF and PAUSE_PROOF for the
narrow live scope; remaining lifecycle, spells, ranks and hardware tests stay open.


EXP-024 records the provenance of native pawn AI animation-19 requests at the
shared parameterized-action queue. A token binds to the first matching state-0
generic action update; simple/prebuilt/unknown requests, cleanup, world changes
and unproven ownership transitions invalidate it. P1 loss while solo retains an
already-bound source/lifetime with a rotated token; stale callbacks cannot use
the previous token. Explicit reassignment/rejoin and a fresh control frame are
still mandatory. Unbound requests do not survive that loss. An inherited AI gesture uses
the native completion byte only at its update return boundary, with current
identity and a fresh controller frame. Native code owns replacement and cleanup.
Already-owned requests from that exact AI caller are refused through the native
failure branch before enqueue. Other sources/arguments and other actors retain
native behavior. Six custom bridges preserve the complete native machine state.
This is deliberately limited to the observed source/animation; broader scripted
and lifecycle acceptance remains required. See GENERIC_ENQUEUE_RESEARCH and the
compiled handoff/owned reports for tested builds and limits.

EXP-022 adds pawn-owned skill slot/rank snapshots at the established actor
callback. The native uGUIActionPallet update copies bounded labels from its live
resource, publishing values only after rechecking actor, epoch, generation and
age. The render consumer requires a matching fresh snapshot and never keeps native
string/resource pointers. Current palettes cover implemented Strider controls,
with empty slots and held-button release feedback.

Text uses GDI Unicode rasterization into a bounded CPU cache, then one D3D9 managed
texture. The texture is reused while content/device/size match; hidden/error paths
release it. Managed-pool textures survive Reset; same-size and resized reset tests
verify rendering, and hiding releases the device reference. Geometry and state
blocks remain transient. No new engine writes/calls or global actor-context swaps
are introduced. See EXP-022 for performance evidence.

EXP-021 routes Strider dagger RB+X/Y/B through the existing actor input consumer
using native palette/slot bits. The actor's equipped skills, action eligibility,
costs and movement remain native. A shared face-button release gate feeds both
palettes, blocks held inputs across active palette changes and bow readiness loss,
and resets during pause/ownership changes even when actor updates are frozen.
Ordinary X is release-gated too, preventing primary input from leaking into light
attacks when RB is released. A failed bow snapshot revokes both palettes' intent.
The verified implementation scope is Strider daggers; other vocations still need
native references, targeting and live acceptance. See PRIMARY_COMPILED_GATE.

EXP-019 intercepts B7CAB1 only for the fresh owned main pawn in native action 57,
resuming at B7CAC6 to skip the AI-selected-target comparison. Native eligibility,
priority and actual target/contact writes remain intact. A second bridge at
B68AA2 applies B68AD8's native player target policy after geometry, avoiding a
pawn-only AI selector mismatch that rejected an actual human contact. Both
bridges require the same fresh ownership and action 57; neither forces native
acceptance or modifies selector state. The contact bridge does not
write the AI pointer. Full GPR/flags/SIMD/x87 state is preserved. Ordinary RT is
release-gated across join, suspension and LB/RB palettes. Native carry is proven;
climbing and other contact actions need separate evidence before extending scope.

EXP-018 suppresses B88650 distance-follow eligibility only for a currently owned
main pawn at the pinned B6D040 return site. A control frame tracks fresh neutral
as well as moving input with identity, epoch and generation. Native support AI,
other placement callers, collision and transitions retain their original paths.
The bridge preserves full GPR/SIMD/x87 state because the native caller retains
XMM values across this function. Leave/loss/suspension/stale ownership restore
native eligibility. This prevents observed AI catch-up from cancelling P2 control;
it does not replace the required streaming boundary or prove unlimited distance.

EXP-017 intercepts the native pawn sprint-cost exemption at B81B8C, after weight,
augment and regional cost calculation. A custom x86 bridge preserves GPRs,
flags, XMM0-7 and x87 across a read-only ownership query. It skips only the pawn
cost-zeroing block for the current actor/epoch/generation with fresh movement,
valid gameplay and healthy offline state. Native resource application and
exhaustion code are unchanged. P1, support pawns and unowned actors take the
original branch. The bridge has a standalone hostile-callback ABI test and live
cost/interruption evidence. Zero-stamina exhaustion entry and recovery are now
observed for both actors; recovery timing, wider terrain/vocations remain open.

The initial split-screen adapter in `src/split_screen.cpp` hooks native camera
matrix update, camera viewport traversal and the synchronous scene draw. View 0
stays attached to the native Arisen camera; view 1 uses an aligned, runtime-owned
camera object. Render eligibility is extended only for the duration of the second
scene draw and restored after native jobs finish. No second simulation update or
additional D3D device is created. Menus and unjoined sessions use vanilla full-screen
presentation. EXP-007 records exact ABI, lifecycle and test limits.

Orbit state follows the actor/scene world epoch, independently of controller
assignment generations. Leave/disconnect restores solo rendering; rejoining the
same pawn retains its chosen yaw/pitch. Actor replacement/destruction and scene
changes invalidate the epoch. Native audio update 0x4AD5D0 enumerates active
viewport cameras and updates their listener matrices; normal world sound events
receive the resulting listener mask. EXP-008 verifies masks 3/1/3 through
split/solo/rejoin without an additional audio hook.

EXP-023 handles a native unload that clears view 1's camera before our restore
boundary. While the same manager is leased, null camera and render-target
pointers plus exact equality to our last-written enabled/layout/rectangle values
permit restoration of those scalar fields only. Native matrices and P1 state are
preserved on this detached path; changed fields or foreign owners prohibit it.
The last-written layout follows resize. Camera Metrics v2 keeps its 48-byte size
and uses the former reserved word for successful detached-restoration count.

EXP-008 adds a native swept-sphere obstruction query at the camera-update
boundary, using private aligned query buffers and the native camera filter.
The P2 near plane remains inside the sweep radius. Native custom rectangles
split the normal 16:9 letterboxed canvas; rectangles are reapplied before render
traversal because sCameraExt changes view 0 after matrix update. Two minimap
draw hooks scale its direct pixel geometry but preserve native offscreen texture
scale, restoring unit fields before the outer draw returns.

Camera errors latch for the process lifetime: restore the solo view, suspend P2
input, return native pawn AI and retain the Offline lock. Assignments are retained
while suspended. Restart is required after a camera fault. A one-shot invalid
private sweep-result test verifies this path; it does not exercise every possible
engine fault. `CoopGetCameraMetrics` exposes size/version-checked values and
bounded 2048-sample timing rings; it does not expose engine pointers or measure
GPU/all-mod overhead.

`Disabled -> Solo -> Joining -> Controlled -> Suspended -> Controlled/Leaving -> Solo`.
Unknown version stays Disabled. Joining requires a valid main pawn and two separate
controller assignments and a verified native/transport offline lock. Controlled
owns voluntary pawn commands only. See OFFLINE_POLICY.md. Menus,
cutscenes, loading, save-critical sections and loss of focus suspend command
injection. AI policy during suspension depends on the native game state: do not
force a paused actor to run. Leaving clears held inputs, restores ownership and
only then releases the actor reference. Every operation is idempotent.

The pawn resource HUD samples native health/stamina values at its existing actor
callback, at most every 100 ms. Values cross the runtime lock without engine
pointers. The render consumer draws only with fresh resources and active split
ownership. It captures/restores D3D state and releases temporary COM resources
on every draw; skill text retains only the reset-safe cache above. `CoopGetHudStatus` exposes
versioned values and bounded submission timings. EXP-012 records getter and render
ABIs, native field evidence, reset and state-restoration tests. The Strider bow
snapshot also carries fresh aim readiness, held-shot gating and the native selected
slot. The overlay renders its reticle at the P2 viewport center and exposes a
separate 32-byte diagnostic ABI. Full skill and assignment/boundary UI remain open.

EXP-015 ground HUD observes the native bow-ground consumer after its original
callback. It queries hit confidence using private collision buffers and publishes
only the native action's final point after ownership/frame revalidation and target
agreement. A tested one-unit query-origin clearance handles rays starting on the
floor; it never changes the engine's actual target. Ground values and the camera's
post-update projection expire after 100 ms and must share epoch/generation. The
HUD clips its cyan marker to P2's pane and distinguishes preparing, unconfirmed,
offscreen and confirmed targets. Separate 64/44-byte diagnostic ABIs preserve the
existing bow/resource interfaces. Broader terrain and combat remain unverified.

EXP-013 adds a Strider bow adapter at the pawn's native B1D010 target consumer.
The camera publishes value-only eye/target data stamped with world epoch,
controller generation and time. The input callback allows draw only with a fresh
view and withholds X/RT until a target has been acquired. Held shots need release
after interrupted readiness. The native action supplies its own range. The query
uses the verified weapon origin and native bow collision filter, outside the
runtime lock; ownership, input frame and freshness are rechecked before writing
the pawn-owned target. Invalid results clear bow intent and disable further
co-op ownership. Native AI, Arisen aim and support pawns retain their own paths.
Initial draw warms up through the native action; this is not a completed
all-vocation targeting system. See EXP-013 for live evidence and limits.

## Required research evidence

EXP-017 reads the actor interface's native walk/run curve and supplies mode 1 or
2 with camera-relative heading. Because the pawn consumer resets speed factors,
the adapter applies matching analog factors immediately after that consumer,
rechecking actor, epoch, controller generation and freshness. No input-mode or
transform change is made. LS supplies the proved sprint-specific 0x4000 bit;
native actions own acceleration, braking and collision. The basic release gate
also blocks LS across ownership/suspension/modifier boundaries. Sprint stamina
cost is verified on the Strider fixture, as is one clear-road steering turn.
Exhaustion recovery timing and wider route/vocation acceptance remain open.

EXP-014 shifts the fresh owned bow camera 65 units right with bounded smoothing.
The existing native sphere sweep constrains the shoulder pivot before the orbit
eye, preventing the offset from starting beyond a wall. Collision-resolved eyes
within 16 units of the look point receive a nondegenerate look vector along the
chosen yaw/pitch. No actor transform or collision result is changed. P2-only
body/attachment hiding also handles a compressed aim ray crossing the torso.
Gameplay health and native Offline diagnostics are separate; routing still
requires every guard. A gameplay fault never releases the network lock.

- Party slot is not enough: distinguish main pawn from support pawns and recycled
  allocations with an identity/generation token.
- A signature hit alone is not enough: verify instruction boundary, surrounding
  control flow, calling convention, stack balance, register preservation and thread.
- Pawn AI includes survival and engine bookkeeping. Do not disable its entire
  update merely to suppress autonomous combat decisions.
- Never infer actor ownership from a global Arisen pointer swap. Player-specific
  targeting, skills and camera helpers may have hidden global state or recursion.
- Memory protection checks reduce invalid accesses but do not prove semantic
  validity. Do not use exception swallowing as the primary safety mechanism.

## Build compatibility

Each supported executable gets a manifest with SHA-256, PE machine, required
signature match counts, hook bytes, relative addresses, ABI notes and evidence.
Use module-relative addresses with runtime range validation. Each multi-hook
change has a rollback list; no partially installed control path is acceptable.
The released-runtime supported-build set remains empty. The internal S2 runtime
supports only the hash/base in STATUS. Its generated manifest records RVAs and
unique signatures; adapter data addresses are fixed for that verified base.
Relocated images, altered executables and newer builds remain unsupported.

## Persistence and extensions

v1 stores preferences outside the game save and uses the existing pawn inventory
and progression. No custom objects or pointers are serialized into DDDA saves.
Before returning to a save boundary, remove transient control state where proven
necessary. Prove normal load both with and without the mod.

Keep `CommandFrame`, `ActorHandle`, `WorldEpoch` and view context separate so later
network input and split views can reuse the actor adapter. The network transport
may replace the command source, but world replication is still a separate system.
Keep camera rendering in its dedicated adapter. Future network threads and
inventory transactions must remain separate from the native actor-input hooks.


## Owned Ingle control-loss cancellation

EXP-027 / MAGE_INGLE_HANDOFF_PROOF: neutral input releases native ready Ingle.
The poller therefore carries a value-only, <=100ms identity token across loss of
control; only the existing pawn button consumer can validate and consume it as
one A edge. Current action/parameters, actor/world/generation and native lifetime
invalidation prevent reuse. Native staff reinit clears it even at the same address.
The token never retains targeting ownership, writes from a worker, or changes
native action state. Invalid/expired/resumed tokens clear without emitting input.
Long pause behavior remains separately verified; the short token cannot span it.

## Evidence rules

Every result names the code commit, game SHA-256, configuration, input provider,
fixture and timestamp. Use four distinct categories: static inspection,
standalone synthetic test, live game with scripted input, and physical-controller
playtest. Passing one category never automatically passes another.

AI owns all pre-release execution. The user's first requested test is a finished
S5 candidate. Do not require user captures or manual memory exploration to advance.

The next latency increment must remain research-only when developer_input is
enabled, preserve the existing controller/native ABIs, and add no game hook.
Acceptance requires separate P1 logical-delivery and P2 movement/button completion
distributions. P2 measurement tokens must cross the original call on that exact
invocation and reject changed actor/world/assignment provenance afterward. A
pending packet or completed consumer is not proof of action eligibility or damage.

clock rollback and histogram overflow before deployment; expose invalid/dropped
outcomes rather than counting only successful latency samples. Then compare
bounded changed-input and held/neutral-refresh cases in the game, including
pause/resume and explicit leave/rejoin. Keep physical input and display latency
outside the synthetic metric's claims. Cumulative histogram bins must be explicit.

representative mixed session. Cover both Strider and Warrior across the integrated
acceptance sessions, with meaningful ownership, offline, lifecycle, save/load,
and install/uninstall checks. Reuse still-applicable evidence; repeat tests for
changed behavior or observed failures. The previous three one-hour sessions,

administrative quotas, not current requirements or completed evidence.

cadence/missed samples, observed frame behavior, input outcomes and crash/stuck-
actor counts. Report each measure's scope and limitations; do not claim a
whole-mod CPU percentile, display delivery, or persistent-growth conclusion from
partial hook timings or sparse samples. Investigate actual sustained growth,
missed cadence, stalls, crashes or stuck actors and report the observed result.

or unintended file modification. Severity 1: crash, persistent loss of control,
unplayable targeting/vocation, input leaking between players or unrecoverable
session. Severity 2: bounded gameplay/UI defect with workaround. Severity 3: polish.

## AI test strategy without physical pads

Add a test-only command provider behind the same normalized input interface;
drive both actors with independent timestamped sequences in the live game. Test
the real engine adapter, not only the C++ fixture. Add lifecycle/event traces and
deterministic assertions around identity, actions and health/stamina changes.
Keep replay tooling out of normal release UI. Use a harness around the actual
XInput boundary for slot/error/edge cases. Record the hardware gap explicitly.

A final candidate may be fully implemented and internally validated while still
awaiting the user's physical acceptance. Label synthetic and physical evidence
separately, disclose any remaining two-controller hardware gap, and never claim
two real controllers were tested if none were available.

## Final user acceptance form

Only supply this with the finished candidate:

- Build version and game version (collected automatically where possible).
- Controller models and connection types.
- Could both players join, move, fight and use equipped skills independently?
- Did camera visibility or aiming make any vocation unplayable?
- Did disconnect, travel, save/load or exit cause a problem?
- If a defect occurred: what happened, location/action, expected behavior and the
  automatically generated diagnostic bundle. Never require a debugger or compiler.

param([ValidateSet('Debug','Release')][string]$Configuration = 'Debug')
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$projectRoot = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$cmake = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath (Join-Path $projectRoot '.tools\cmake') -Filter cmake.exe -Recurse | Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty FullName
if (!$cmake) { throw 'Run scripts/bootstrap_tools.py first.' }
$build = Join-Path $projectRoot 'build\win32'
& $cmake -S $projectRoot -B $build -G 'Visual Studio 17 2022' -A Win32
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'CMake configuration failed.' }
& $cmake --build $build --config $Configuration --parallel 4
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Build failed.' }
$ctest = Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent $cmake) 'ctest.exe'
$reports = Join-Path $projectRoot 'artifacts\tests'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $reports -Force | Out-Null
& $ctest --test-dir $build -C $Configuration --output-on-failure --output-junit (Join-Path $reports "$Configuration.xml")
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Tests failed.' }
